correctness.rationale: Complete proof: every nontrivial tree forces at least one agent with zero valued own items and hence envy; orientation away from tree roots and around cycles attains exactly that count with maximum welfare. Nonenvy from a positive incoming edge relies on graph simplicity. For G(n,p), the exact isolated-edge factorial moment tends to (e^-c/4)^r, and expectations of all larger tree components vanish by fixed-size, geometric and Chernoff/union-bound estimates. Executable finite checker passed 1099 endpoint graphs and 75 unrestricted assignment graphs; finite experiments are not treated as infinite proof.
